organizations.normalization_notes: Preserved as the named federal organization. Houts's earlier government assignment and Campisi's immediate government affiliation and last named civilian employer remain separate claim-level relationships; government-assignment records remain outside employment-only analytics.

affiliations.date_precision: The official memorandum says FBI employment ran 1941-1946 and that OSS service in 1944-1946 occurred while Campisi was on military leave from the FBI.
affiliations.research_notes: The official source explicitly calls Campisi an FBI employee and states that his OSS service was performed while on military leave from the FBI. The FBI is therefore both the immediate pre-OSS government affiliation and the last named civilian employer. No special-agent title is inferred.

affiliations.date_precision: The official Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 747 on November 12, 1942; no employer, port, dock, union, or workplace is named.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier and exact full name confirm identity. The plural occupational category follows the official code list and identifies no employer, port, dock, union, workplace, exact duties, or later Army-to-OSS sequence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Joseph F. Campisi is a high-confidence match to the FBI employee whom an official CIA memorandum places in OSS service in the United Kingdom from 1944 to 1946.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The unusual exact full name appears in both the OSS personnel index and a person-specific official memorandum that explicitly documents OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an uncommon exact full name and an exceptionally specific official source explicitly linking that person to OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorandum dates FBI employment to 1941-1946 and OSS service to 1944-1946.
claims.match_notes: The index lacks a rank and private identifier, so the identity is high confidence rather than confirmed. The personnel file remains the final direct cross-check.

claims.claim_text: Joseph F. Campisi's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Federal Bureau of Investigation, from which he was on military leave while serving with OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: on military leave from the FBI, serving with OSS
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official memorandum directly describes the FBI-to-OSS relationship and dates it to 1944-1946.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence exact-name identity supported by a person-specific official OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate relationship: OSS service occurred while Campisi remained an FBI employee on military leave.
claims.match_notes: The relationship is classified as a government assignment. No FBI title, military branch, or OSS function is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Joseph F. Campisi's last documented civilian employer before OSS service was the Federal Bureau of Investigation; the official source does not state his title.
claims.evidence_excerpt: From 1941-46, Subject was employed by the FBI.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An official memorandum explicitly names the FBI as Campisi's employer and says OSS service began during military leave from that employment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence exact-name identity supported by a person-specific official OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The FBI employment began in 1941 and continued through the 1944 start of OSS service, establishing the last named civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: This is a federal-government employer, separately labeled as a government assignment. No earlier private employer is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Michael J. Campo is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact private-identifier and exact full-name match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS index and official Army-entry file share an exact private identifier and exact full name; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private identifier and exact full name across two official records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated November 12, 1942; later OSS chronology is not established.
claims.match_notes: A second exact-name Army row exists with a different identifier; only the exact-identifier record was accepted.
